mainTopic: Blowing שופר on שבת only with the בית דין (time or place), and רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactments of לולב and יום הנף as a זכר למקדש
overview: The גמרא explains רב הונא's phrase "ועם בית דין": in יבנה, the שופר was blown on שבת only in front of the בית דין. רבא challenges this from the משנה's words "ועוד זאת", but the גמרא answers that ירושלים's extra advantage was that it blew even away from the court. In a second version, רב הונא's words mean the court's hours. רבא and רב ששת challenge this version from two ברייתות, and the גמרא answers each challenge: the יובל שופר may be blown away from the court, but only while it is in session. A teaching of רבי supports this, and רבי זירא's question about judges who began to rise ends in תיקו. The גמרא then explains the four conditions for towns near ירושלים. A new משנה lists רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactments: לולב for seven days everywhere as a זכר למקדש, and a ban on new grain for the whole יום הנף. The גמרא gives a פסוק as the source for זכר למקדש and a reason for the יום הנף ban. רב נחמן בר יצחק then begins a different explanation, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What does "with the court" mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the phrase "ועם בית דין" from the previous statement and asks what it means.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And with the court." What does "and with the court" mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא picks up a short, unclear phrase from רב הונא's statement about blowing שופר on שבת in יבנה and asks what it means. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "With the court" could mean several things, such as at the same time as the court or in the same place as the court. The גמרא wants a precise definition before going further, because the coming challenge depends on it.

keyTerms.meaning: The court; here, the great court that sat in יבנה
What? (asking for the meaning of something)

phrases.english: "And with the court."
What does "and with the court" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the clarification of רב הונא's phrase from the previous part of the daf.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact meaning of "with the court" in רב הונא's statement.

steps.title: It means in front of the court
steps.stepSummary: "With the court" means in the presence of the בית דין. Away from the בית דין, the שופר was not blown.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means in the presence of the court. This excludes a place not in the presence of the court, where they did not blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that "with the court" means physically in front of the בית דין. Anywhere else in יבנה, the שופר was not blown on שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns רב הונא's rule into a rule about place. Being in the same town is not enough; you had to be where the בית דין actually sat. This is the claim רבא will now attack.

keyTerms.meaning: In front of, in the presence of

phrases.english: In the presence of the court,

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין — דְּלָא.
phrases.english: to exclude a place not in the presence of the court, where they do not blow.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין, לְאַפּוֹקֵי שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "With the court" means in the physical presence of the בית דין. Places not in its presence are excluded.
steps.whyThisMatters: This place-based reading of רב הונא is exactly what רבא's objection will try to disprove.

steps.title: רבא objects from the משנה's "this additional"
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens an objection by quoting the משנה: "And this additional thing ירושלים had over יבנה."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא raised an objection: "And this additional thing ירושלים had over יבנה, etc."
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins a challenge to רב הונא by quoting a line from the משנה. This step only sets up the objection; the argument is built in the steps that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The line comes from the משנה that lists ways ירושלים was better than יבנה for blowing שופר on שבת. רבא will focus on the extra word "ועוד" ("additional") to show a hidden law.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a משנה or ברייתא
רבא, a leading אמורא of Babylonia
יבנה, the town where the סנהדרין sat after the Temple was destroyed

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
"And this additional thing Jerusalem had
over Yavne, etc."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins an attack on the definition given in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that in יבנה the שופר was blown on שבת only in the presence of the בית דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה's word "ועוד" will be shown to imply a law in יבנה that conflicts with רב הונא.

steps.title: What does "this additional" mean?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks what the משנה means by "ועוד זאת", an extra advantage of ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is "and this additional"?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks what extra advantage the word "ועוד" is pointing to. He is setting up a close reading of the משנה's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "ועוד" suggests that ירושלים had some advantage beyond the one the משנה spells out. רבא wants to find that hidden advantage.

keyTerms.meaning: And this additional thing, and this too

phrases.english: What is "and this additional"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the משנה phrase quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which extra advantage the word "ועוד" refers to.

steps.title: It cannot mean only what the משנה spells out
steps.stepSummary: If "ועוד זאת" meant only the advantage the משנה states openly, the משנה would have said just "זאת".
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means what the משנה teaches, it should have said just "this."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the simple reading. If the משנה meant only the advantage it lists, the word "ועוד" would be extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה does not waste words. So "ועוד" must point to an extra advantage of ירושלים that is not written out. This forces the search for a hidden law.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say it means just what it teaches,
it should have said just "this."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the simplest answer to step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that "ועוד זאת" refers only to the advantage written in the משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It leaves the word "ועוד" with nothing to teach.

steps.title: First suggestion: individuals could blow in ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: Suggestion: the extra advantage is that in ירושלים individuals blew the שופר on שבת, while in יבנה they did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: in ירושלים individuals blow, and in יבנה individuals do not blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a hidden advantage: in ירושלים even private people could blow שופר on שבת, but in יבנה they could not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This would give "ועוד" a meaning without contradicting רב הונא. It turns out to be a temporary answer, because the next step shows that individuals did blow in יבנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Individuals, private people (not the official שליח ציבור)

phrases.english: Rather: in Jerusalem individuals blow,
and in Yavne individuals do not blow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to step 4 after step 5 rejected the simple one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: "ועוד" means that individuals could blow in ירושלים but not in יבנה.

steps.title: But individuals did blow in Yavne
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reported that after the שליח ציבור finished blowing in יבנה, the blasts of individuals were so loud that no one could hear himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in יבנה individuals do not blow? But when רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: When the community's agent finished blowing in יבנה, a person could not hear his own voice because of the sound of the individuals blowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא knocks down the suggestion of step 6. An eyewitness report shows that many individuals blew שופר in יבנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If private people blew loudly in יבנה, then "individuals may blow" cannot be what made ירושלים better. The meaning of "ועוד" is open again.

keyTerms.meaning: The שליח ציבור, the one who leads and blows for the community

phrases.english: And in Yavne individuals do not blow?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף, אָמַר:
phrases.english: But when Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef came, he said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי מְסַיֵּים שְׁלִיחָא דְצִיבּוּרָא תְּקִיעָה בְּיַבְנֶה —
phrases.english: When the community's agent finished the blowing in Yavne,
a person could not hear the sound of his own ear
phrases.notes: He means it was so loud that you couldn't even hear yourself.

phrases.english: because of the sound of the individuals' blowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that individuals did not blow שופר in יבנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An eyewitness report says individuals in יבנה blew so loudly that no one could hear himself.

steps.title: The real difference is timing, which contradicts רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The difference must be that ירושלים blew at any time, while יבנה blew only while the בית דין was in session. So יבנה blew during court time even away from the בית דין, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not that in ירושלים they blow both during the court's time and not during the court's time, while in יבנה, during the court's time, yes, and not during the court's time, no? So during the court's time, at least, they blow, even not in the presence of the court!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא finishes his objection. "ועוד" means ירושלים had no time limit, while יבנה blew only while the בית דין was in session. That allowed blowing anywhere in town during that time, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule in יבנה turns out to depend on when the court is sitting, not where. Since individuals all over יבנה blew during court hours, the שופר was blown even away from the בית דין. This directly contradicts the definition in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (introduces the forced conclusion)
During the time the court is in session

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא said that in יבנה the שופר was blown on שבת only in front of the בית דין. רבא reads "ועוד זאת" in the משנה to mean that יבנה limited the blowing by time, not place. So during court hours it was blown even away from the court, which contradicts רב הונא.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין (in front of the court, a place rule) with בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין (while the court is in session, a time rule). The whole objection depends on this difference.
steps.whyThisMatters: This step introduces the time-versus-place question that the rest of the sugya will have to answer for רב הונא.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not that in Jerusalem they blow
both during the court's time
and not during the court's time,
while in Yavne, during the court's time, yes,
and not during the court's time, no?

phrases.aramaic: הָא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין מִיהָא תּוֹקְעִין,
phrases.english: So during the court's time, at least, they blow,
even not in the presence of the court!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו: דְּבִירוּשָׁלַיִם תּוֹקְעִין בֵּין בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a new answer to step 4 after step 7 refuted step 6, then turns it into the final challenge to step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule (step 2) that in יבנה the שופר was blown only in front of the בית דין.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If יבנה's rule was about the court's hours, then during those hours people blew anywhere in town, including away from the court. That contradicts a place-based rule.

steps.title: The difference is being in front of the court, not the time of day
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the claim of step 8. The difference between ירושלים and יבנה is about being in front of the בית דין, not about the court's hours. This fits רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. In ירושלים they blew both in front of the בית דין and away from it. In יבנה, in front of the בית דין, yes; away from the בית דין, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last step and gives a different meaning for 'ועוד זאת'. The extra advantage of ירושלים is that they blew even away from the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 said the difference was about time, which would mean יבנה blew away from the court, against רב הונא. Now the גמרא says the difference is about place, being in front of the court or not. So in יבנה they blew only in front of the בית דין, just as רב הונא said.

keyTerms.meaning: In the presence of the court
Not in the presence of the court

phrases.english: No: whereas in Jerusalem they would blow
phrases.notes: He means blowing the שופר on שבת.

phrases.english: both in the presence of the court
and not in the presence of the court,
and in Yavne, in the presence of the court, yes,
not in the presence of the court, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא: דְּאִילּוּ בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם תּוֹקְעִין בֵּין בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 8's reading and replaces it with one that fits רב הונא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The idea that the ירושלים/יבנה difference was about the court's hours.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The difference can be about presence in front of the court instead, so there is no contradiction with רב הונא.
steps.whatToRemember: In this version, ירושלים blew on שבת anywhere, and יבנה blew only in front of the בית דין.

steps.title: A second version: רב הונא's words go on the יובל שופר
steps.stepSummary: Some teach רב הונא's statement on a ברייתא about the יובל שופר. The ברייתא says every individual must blow, and רב הונא adds 'and with the בית דין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some teach רב הונא's statement on this: it is written, 'On יום הכפורים you shall sound the שופר throughout all your land.' This teaches that every single person must blow. רב הונא said: and together with the בית דין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a different version of where רב הונא said his words. This sets up a question about what 'with the בית דין' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רב הונא was explaining the משנה about יבנה. In this version, he adds a limit to the ברייתא about the יובל, where every person blows. His limit is 'ועם בית דין', and that phrase is unclear, so the next step asks about it.

phrases.english: Some teach this statement of Rav Huna
on this, as it is written:
"On Yom Kippur you shall sound the shofar
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:9. This is the שופר of the יובל year.

phrases.english: throughout all your land"
This teaches that each and every individual
is obligated to blow.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: וְעִם בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: Rav Huna said: And with the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא אַהָא דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second version of רב הונא's statement, attached to a different source.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every individual must blow the יובל שופר, and according to רב הונא, together with the בית דין.

steps.title: What does 'with the court' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב הונא meant by 'with the בית דין'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and with the בית דין' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of רב הונא's short phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'With the court' could mean in the same place as the court or at the same time as the court. The גמרא wants to know which one he meant.

keyTerms.meaning: What is / what does it mean

phrases.english: What is 'and with the court'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what רב הונא's words in step 10 mean.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'with the court' means place or time.

steps.title: It means during the court's hours
steps.stepSummary: 'With the בית דין' means while the court is in session. When the court is not in session, people do not blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means at the time the בית דין is sitting. This leaves out a time when the בית דין is not sitting: then they do not blow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רב הונא was talking about time, not place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this second version, a person may blow even away from the court, but only during the hours the court is in session. This is a different limit from step 9, which was about being in front of the court.

keyTerms.meaning: While the court is in session

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, רב הונא's limit is being in front of the court. In this one, it is the court's hours.

phrases.english: At the time of the court.

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין, דְּלָא.
phrases.english: To exclude a time when the court is not in session, when they do not blow.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין. לְאַפּוֹקֵי שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין, דְּלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It refers to time: blowing is allowed only while the court is in session.

steps.title: רבא challenges from 'every man and his house'
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a ברייתא: the שופר of ראש השנה and of the יובל overrides שבת even outside the מקדש, 'every man and his house'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא challenged: The blowing of ראש השנה and of the יובל overrides שבת even in the outlying areas, every man and his house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts a challenge to רב הונא's second version. The key words 'איש וביתו' will be examined in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seems to let people blow broadly, in their own homes. That may not fit רב הונא's limit of the court's hours, but the challenge only becomes clear once the גמרא works out what 'איש וביתו' means.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source

phrases.english: Rava raised an objection:
The blowing of Rosh HaShana and of the Jubilee
overrides Shabbat in the outlying areas,
every man and his house.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵתִיב רָבָא: תְּקִיעַת רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה וְיוֹבֵל דּוֹחָה אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת בִּגְבוּלִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule given in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule (second version) that one blows only while the court is in session.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא lets every man blow on שבת, seemingly with no time limit.

steps.title: What does 'every man and his house' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the words 'איש וביתו' mean.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'every man and his house' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to work out the meaning of the key words in רבא's ברייתא. This sets up the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whether רבא's challenge works depends on what 'איש וביתו' means, so the גמרא checks the possible readings one by one.

phrases.english: What is "every man and his house"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the ברייתא in step 13.

steps.title: It cannot mean a man and his wife
steps.stepSummary: If 'his house' meant his wife, that would make a woman obligated. But שופר is a time-bound positive מצוה, and women are exempt from those.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means a man and his wife, is a woman obligated? שופר is a מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא, and women are exempt from every מצות עשה שהזמן גרמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first possible meaning, 'a man and his wife', and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ביתו' often means a man's wife. But a woman is exempt from שופר, because it is a positive מצוה tied to a set time. So the ברייתא cannot be saying she is included.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive מצוה tied to a set time

phrases.english: If you say it means a man and his wife,
is a woman obligated?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא מִצְוַת עֲשֵׂה שֶׁהַזְּמַן גְּרָמָא הִיא,
phrases.english: But it is a positive מצוה caused by time,
and from every positive מצוה caused by time,
women are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא אִישׁ וְאִשְׁתּוֹ — אִיתְּתָא מִי מִיחַיְּיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects one answer to step 14's question.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Women are exempt from time-bound positive מצוות such as שופר.

steps.title: So it means each man at home, even outside court hours
steps.stepSummary: The only reading left is 'every man in his house', which seems to allow blowing even when the court is not in session. That goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean every man in his house, and even when the בית דין is not in session?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבא's challenge is complete. The ברייתא seems to let each person blow at home with no time limit, against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once 'his wife' is ruled out, 'ביתו' must mean 'his home'. A man blowing in his own home sounds unconnected to the court's schedule, which goes against רב הונא's limit from step 12.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not: every man in his house,
and even when the court is not in session!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לָאו: אִישׁ בְּבֵיתוֹ, וַאֲפִילּוּ שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge begun in step 13, using the reading left after step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blowing in one's own home seems to be allowed even when the court is not in session.

steps.title: Still only during court hours
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers: a man may blow in his house, but only while the בית דין is in session.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It still means only when the בית דין is in session.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא. 'In his house' tells us where a person may blow, not when.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא allows blowing at home, away from the court, but it never said this is allowed at any hour. So the court's hours can still be the limit, and רב הונא stands.
steps.whatToRemember: In the second version, רב הונא allows blowing at home on שבת, but only during the hours the בית דין is in session.

phrases.english: No, it is actually at a time when the court is in session.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the source: the ברייתא is about where one blows, not when.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Every man in his house' meant blowing at any time.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blowing at home is allowed only while the court is in session, so רב הונא stands.

steps.title: רב ששת quotes a ברייתא comparing the יובל and ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת brings a ברייתא. On the יובל, שופר is blown in any court and every individual must blow. On ראש השנה, it is blown only in the court that sanctified the month, and not every individual must blow.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת objected: the יובל is like ראש השנה for the שופר blowing and the extra blessings. But on the יובל they blow both in the court that sanctified the month and in a court that did not, and every single person must blow. On ראש השנה they blew only in the court that sanctified the month, and not every single person must blow.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת opens a new challenge against רב הונא by quoting a ברייתא. The actual attack only becomes clear in the next steps, once the גמרא works out what the ברייתא means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists two differences between the יובל and ראש השנה: which court may blow, and whether every individual must blow. The second difference, 'not every individual,' is unclear. The גמרא will dig into it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection, usually from a ברייתא or משנה
The Jubilee (50th) year. Here it means its יום כיפור, when shofar is blown
The special blessings added to the שמונה עשרה (מלכויות, זכרונות, שופרות)
An individual person, as opposed to the court or the community

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet raised an objection:
The Jubilee is the same as Rosh Hashanah
phrases.notes: This means יום כיפור of the יובל year, the day the shofar is blown that year.

phrases.english: for the shofar blowing and for the blessings,
except that on the Jubilee they blow

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בּוֹ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: both in the court in which they sanctified the month,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵין בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁלֹּא קִידְּשׁוּ בּוֹ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: and in a court in which they did not sanctify the month,
and each and every individual is obligated to blow.
On Rosh Hashanah they would not blow

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בְּבֵית דִּין שֶׁקִּידְּשׁוּ בּוֹ אֶת הַחֹדֶשׁ,
phrases.english: except in the court in which they sanctified the month,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין כׇּל יָחִיד וְיָחִיד חַיָּיב לִתְקוֹעַ.
phrases.english: and each and every individual is not obligated to blow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the answer in step 17, a new objection to רב הונא's view is introduced.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that שופר (when it overrides שבת) is blown only while the בית דין is in session
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא suggests the יובל שופר is blown even outside the court's setting. The גמרא will sharpen this into 'even when the court is not in session.'

steps.title: What does 'not every individual must blow' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the unclear phrase and offers a first reading: on ראש השנה, individuals did not blow at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'not every individual is obligated to blow' mean? Suppose you say it means that on the יובל individuals blow, but on ראש השנה individuals do not blow at all.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא's last phrase means. It suggests a first, simple reading, which it is about to knock down.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simplest reading is that individuals were not allowed to blow on ראש השנה. This is only a trial reading (אילימא), set up so it can be tested.

keyTerms.meaning: 'If you say...' introduces a suggested reading that will usually be rejected

phrases.aramaic: מַאי אֵין כׇּל יָחִיד וְיָחִיד חַיָּיב לִתְקוֹעַ?
phrases.english: What does 'each and every individual is not obligated to blow' mean?
If you say that on the Jubilee individuals blow
but on Rosh Hashanah individuals do not blow,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי אֵין כׇּל יָחִיד וְיָחִיד חַיָּיב לִתְקוֹעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the unclear last clause of the ברייתא quoted in step 18.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'not every individual is obligated to blow' on ראש השנה

steps.title: In יבנה individuals did blow on ראש השנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר יוסף reported that in יבנה, after the חזן finished blowing, the many individuals blowing made so much noise that no one could hear himself. So individuals did blow on ראש השנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But when רב יצחק בר יוסף came, he said: when the חזן finished the blowing in יבנה, a person could not hear his own voice because of the noise of individuals blowing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the first reading from step 19. It proves from a real report that individuals did blow on ראש השנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If individuals never blew on ראש השנה, there could not have been a loud crowd of individuals blowing in יבנה. So 'not every individual' cannot mean individuals were not allowed to blow.

keyTerms.meaning: When he came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
The town where the סנהדרין sat after the חורבן

phrases.english: But when he came,
Rav Yitzchak bar Yosef said:
When the prayer leader would finish
the shofar blasts in Yavne,
a person could not hear the sound in his own ear
phrases.notes: He means it was so loud you couldn't even hear yourself.

phrases.english: because of the noise of the individuals' blowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב יִצְחָק בַּר יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the trial reading offered in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The reading that individuals did not blow at all on ראש השנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It contradicts the report from יבנה, where many individuals blew on ראש השנה.

steps.title: So the יובל שופר is blown even when the court is not in session
steps.stepSummary: The only remaining reading is about timing. On the יובל they blow even when the court is not in session, while on ראש השנה they blow only while it is in session. That goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, doesn't it mean this: on the יובל they blow both while the court is in session and when it is not, but on ראש השנה, while the court is in session, yes, and when it is not, no? In any case, the ברייתא teaches that on the יובל they blow even when the court is not in session!
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first reading failed, the גמרא proposes a reading about the court's time. That reading turns the ברייתא into a real challenge to רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the יובל שופר may be blown even when the court is not sitting. That contradicts רב הונא, who holds that שופר is blown only while the court is in session. The phrase קתני מיהת points to the exact words that cause the trouble.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Rather, isn't it...' gives the remaining possible reading
During the time the court is in session
'In any case it teaches...' points to the part of the source that causes the problem

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it
that while on the Jubilee they blow
both during the court's time
and not during the court's time,

phrases.aramaic: וּבְרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה, בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין — אֵין,
phrases.english: but on Rosh Hashanah, during the court's time, yes,
not during the court's time, no.
In any case, it teaches: on the Jubilee

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין, בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין!
phrases.english: both during the court's time and not during the court's time!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the reading in step 19 was rejected, this offers the remaining reading and turns it into an attack.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that שופר is blown only while the בית דין is in session
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא, read this way, explicitly allows the יובל שופר even when the court is not in session.

steps.title: The difference is being in front of the court, not the court's time
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the שופר of both days is blown only while the court is in session. On the יובל it may be blown away from the court. On ראש השנה it must be blown in front of the court.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really, it is only while the court is in session, and this is what the ברייתא teaches. On the יובל, while the court is in session, they blow both in front of the court and not in front of the court. On ראש השנה they blow while the court is in session and in front of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by reading the ברייתא differently. It still keeps 'only while the court is in session' for both days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's difference is about place, not time. בזמן בית דין (while the court is sitting) applies to both days. בפני בית דין (in the court's presence) is required only on ראש השנה. So the ברייתא never allows blowing when the court is not sitting.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Really, actually' keeps the original position while explaining the source
'And this is what it teaches' introduces a new reading of the source
In the presence of the court

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up בזמן בית דין (while the court is sitting, a matter of time) with בפני בית דין (in front of the court, a matter of place). The whole answer depends on the difference between them.

phrases.english: No, really it is only during the court's time,
and this is what it teaches:
On the Jubilee, during the court's time, they blow

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין, בֵּין שֶׁלֹּא בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: both in the presence of the court and not in the presence of the court.
On Rosh Hashanah they blow

phrases.aramaic: בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין, וּבִפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: during the court's time and in the presence of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם בִּזְמַן בֵּית דִּין, וְהָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא allows the יובל שופר even when the court is not in session.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both require the court to be in session. Only ראש השנה requires blowing in the court's presence.

steps.title: רבי: שופר is blown only while the court is sitting
steps.stepSummary: A statement passed down from רבי supports רב הונא: שופר is blown only as long as the בית דין is sitting.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: רבי חייא בר גמדא said in the name of רבי יוסי בן שאול in the name of רבי: they blow only as long as the בית דין is sitting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an outside statement that agrees with רב הונא's position and with the answer just given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: איתמר נמי means 'it was also said,' so the statement backs up what came before. רבי's ruling ties שופר blowing to the time the court is sitting, just as רב הונא said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It was also stated' introduces support from another teacher
רבי יהודה הנשיא, compiler of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב הונא, supported by רבי, שופר (when it overrides שבת) is blown only while the בית דין is in session. On ראש השנה it must also be blown in the court's presence.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the defense of רב הונא. A ברייתא that seemed to argue against him actually fits his rule, and a teaching of רבי directly supports it.

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Rabbi Chiya bar Gamda said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן שָׁאוּל אָמַר רַבִּי:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Yosei ben Shaul said that Rabbi said:
They blow only
as long as the court is sitting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 22 and רב הונא's view.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that שופר is blown only while the בית דין is in session
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי, as passed down by רבי יוסי בן שאול and רבי חייא בר גמדא

steps.title: Judges who started to get up but stayed seated
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא asks whether שופר may still be blown if the judges began to rise but did not actually stand. The question is left unresolved: תיקו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: if the judges stirred to get up but did not actually stand, what is the law? Do we need the court to be sitting, and they still are? Or do we need it to be the court's session time, and that time is over? The question stands unanswered.
steps.whatsHappening: Building on רבי's rule that שופר is blown only while the בית דין sits, רבי זירא asks about an in-between case. The גמרא finds no answer and ends with תיקו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is what the rule really depends on. If it depends on the judges physically sitting, blowing is allowed, because they are still seated. If it depends on the court's session, blowing is not allowed, because by getting ready to leave they have already ended the session.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question that needs an answer)
They stirred themselves or got ready (to get up)
Let it stand: the question stays unresolved

steps.confusionAlert: תיקו does not mean the answer is 'no.' It means the גמרא could not decide either way.

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira asked:
If they stirred to stand but did not stand, what is the law?
phrases.notes: 'They' are the judges of the בית דין. They started getting up to leave but were still in their seats.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית דִּין יוֹשְׁבִין בָּעֵינַן — וְהָא אִיכָּא,
phrases.english: Do we require the court to be sitting? That is the case here.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: זְמַן בֵּית דִּין בָּעֵינַן — וְלֵיכָּא?
phrases.english: Or perhaps we require the court's session time, and that is not the case here?
Let it stand unresolved.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: It tests the edge of the rule just supported by רבי (step 23): שופר is blown only while the בית דין sits.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule depend on the judges physically sitting, or on the court's session still being in progress?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No answer is given. The question ends in תיקו.

steps.title: Explaining the four conditions for towns near Jerusalem
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about ירושלים's advantage over יבנה and explains what each condition (sees, hears, near, can come) leaves out.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said ירושלים had another advantage over יבנה. 'Sees' leaves out a town in a valley. 'Hears' leaves out a town on a mountaintop. 'Near' leaves out a town beyond the תחום. 'Can come' leaves out a town cut off by a river.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the משנה and explains its four conditions one by one. For each condition it names the kind of town that fails it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condition is needed on its own, because a town can pass one test and fail another. A valley town can hear but cannot see. A mountaintop town can see but cannot hear. A town beyond the תחום can see and hear but is too far away. A town across a river may be close but its people cannot actually come.
steps.whatToRemember: Towns around ירושלים could blow שופר on שבת only if all four conditions were true: they could see ירושלים, hear from it, were near it, and could come to it.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד זֹאת הָיְתָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יְתֵירָה עַל יַבְנֶה וְכוּ׳.
phrases.english: And Jerusalem had this further advantage over Yavne, etc.
'Sees' excludes a town that sits in a valley.
'Hears' excludes a town that sits on a mountaintop.
'Near' excludes a town that sits outside the boundary.
phrases.notes: The boundary here is the תחום, how far a person may walk from ירושלים on שבת.

phrases.aramaic: וִיכוֹלָה לָבוֹא — פְּרָט לְמַפְסֵיק לַהּ נַהֲרָא.
phrases.english: 'And can come' excludes a town that a river separates.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד זֹאת הָיְתָה יְרוּשָׁלַיִם יְתֵירָה עַל יַבְנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the בית דין topic ends, the גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the four conditions leaves out a different kind of town: a valley town (cannot see), a mountaintop town (cannot hear), a town beyond the תחום (not near), and a town cut off by a river (cannot come).

steps.title: New משנה: taking the לולב all seven days after the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה says that once, לולב was taken seven days in the מקדש but only one day elsewhere. After the destruction, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי made it seven days everywhere, as a reminder of the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, the לולב was taken for seven days in the מקדש and for one day in the rest of the country. After the מקדש was destroyed, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי ruled that the לולב should be taken in the rest of the country for seven days, as a reminder of the מקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It records another תקנה of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, this time about לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two stages. While the מקדש stood, seven days of לולב happened only in the מקדש, and everywhere else people took it just on the first day. After the destruction, רבן יוחנן בן זכאי spread the seven-day practice everywhere so people would remember how it was done in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: The palm branch taken on סוכות
The country, meaning outside the מקדש

steps.whyThisMatters: This תקנה is the reason we take the לולב all seven days of סוכות today.

phrases.english: MISHNA: At first, the lulav was taken
in the Temple for seven days, and in the country for one day.
Once the Temple was destroyed,
Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted
that the lulav be taken in the country for seven days,
as a reminder of the Temple.

steps.triggerLanguage: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיָה הַלּוּלָב נִיטָּל בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ שִׁבְעָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: It starts a new משנה that continues the list of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's תקנות after the destruction.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After the destruction, לולב is taken all seven days everywhere, as a reminder of the מקדש.

steps.title: Second enactment: the whole day of waving is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The משנה adds another enactment of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי: eating new grain is forbidden for the entire יום הנף.
steps.simpleTranslation: And [he also enacted] that the whole day of waving [the עומר] is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes its list of enactments from after the destruction. רבן יוחנן בן זכאי also made the entire יום הנף forbidden for eating new grain.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'ו' at the start ties this line to the enactment about לולב in the previous step. This is a second takanah made after the destruction. The משנה only says 'forbidden' and does not give the reason yet. The גמרא will explain the reason below.

keyTerms.meaning: The day the עומר offering was waved: the 16th of ניסן
The barley offering brought on the 16th of ניסן, which permits eating new grain
Grain from the new crop, which may not be eaten until the עומר permits it

phrases.english: And that the entire day of waving should be forbidden.
phrases.notes: He means eating the new grain is forbidden all day long. The משנה doesn't spell out what is forbidden, but that's the topic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactments after the לולב enactment.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Eating new grain is forbidden for the whole 16th of ניסן, by rabbinic enactment.

steps.title: Where do we learn to act as a זכר למקדש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source that we do things as a זכר למקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And from where do we know that we do things as a reminder of the בית המקדש?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks a question about the לולב enactment from step 26. That enactment was made as a זכר למקדש, and the גמרא wants to know where that idea comes from. This sets up the next step, where it brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 26 said that רבן יוחנן בן זכאי extended לולב to seven days as a זכר למקדש. The גמרא wants a source for that whole concept. It is not asking about לולב specifically.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do we know?
A reminder of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: GEMARA:
And from where do we know that we act as a reminder of the Temple?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the לולב enactment (step 26) to find the source for זכר למקדש.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A scriptural source for the practice of doing things as a זכר למקדש.

steps.title: The verse: Zion needs to be sought out
steps.stepSummary: The source is ירמיהו's פסוק that ציון has 'no one seeking her'. This implies she should be sought out.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: 'For I will bring healing to you and heal your wounds, says ה׳, because they called you an outcast: She is ציון, no one seeks her out.' From this we learn that ציון needs to be sought out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק from ירמיהו. The פסוק complains that no one seeks out ציון, so we learn that we must seek her out and keep her memory alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof is an inference. The פסוק describes it as a bad thing that ציון 'has no one seeking her'. So the right thing is to seek her out. Actions done as a זכר למקדש are one way of doing that.

keyTerms.meaning: One who seeks out or cares for
Being sought out and cared for

steps.whatToRemember: We do things as a זכר למקדש because the פסוק implies that ציון must be sought out and not forgotten.

phrases.english: As the verse says:
"For I will bring up healing for you,
and I will heal you of your wounds, says the Lord,
because they called you an outcast:
She is Zion, there is no one who seeks her out."
This implies that she needs to be sought out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 28.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ירמיהו 30:17: 'ציון... no one seeks her out' implies she must be sought out, so we do things as a זכר למקדש.

steps.title: Why forbid the whole day of waving?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the second enactment again and asks for its reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] And that the whole יום הנף is forbidden. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the second enactment from the משנה (step 27) and asks why it was made. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without a בית המקדש there is no עומר, so the new grain should become permitted at dawn on the 16th. The גמרא asks why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade it for the whole day anyway.

phrases.english: And that the entire day of waving should be forbidden.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשֶׁיְּהֵא יוֹם הֶנֶף כּוּלּוֹ אָסוּר. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the source for זכר למקדש to the reason for the יום הנף enactment.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade new grain for the entire 16th of ניסן.

steps.title: The worry: people will eat at dawn after the בית המקדש is rebuilt
steps.stepSummary: The reason is that the בית המקדש may be rebuilt soon. People would remember eating new grain at dawn last year and do the same again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Soon the בית המקדש will be rebuilt, and people will say: 'Last year, didn't we eat as soon as the east lit up? Now too let us eat.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the enactment protects against a future mistake. When the בית המקדש is rebuilt, people may copy last year's habit and eat new grain at dawn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The enactment looks forward to the future. If people grow used to eating at dawn now, they will keep doing it after the rebuilding, when it will be forbidden. Forbidding the whole day now prevents that habit from forming.

phrases.english: Soon the Temple will be rebuilt,
and people will say: Last year,
didn't we eat once the east lit up?
Now too, let us eat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מאי טעמא of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The enactment prevents people from eating at dawn by habit once the בית המקדש is rebuilt.

steps.title: Why the habit would be a mistake
steps.stepSummary: Last year there was no עומר, so dawn permitted the grain. Once there is a עומר, only the עומר permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they will not know that last year there was no עומר, so dawn permitted [the new grain]. Now that there is a עומר, the עומר is what permits it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its explanation by showing exactly where people would go wrong. What permits the new grain changes once the עומר is brought again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two different things that permit new grain. Without a בית המקדש, dawn of the 16th permits it. With a בית המקדש, only bringing the עומר permits it. People copying last year's practice would eat before the עומר was brought, which would be forbidden.
steps.whatToRemember: With no עומר, dawn permits new grain. With a עומר, only the עומר permits it. Forbidding the whole day keeps people from building the wrong habit.
steps.confusionAlert: According to this explanation, the enactment does not say the grain is forbidden today by Torah law. It is a rabbinic safeguard aimed at the time when the בית המקדש is rebuilt. רב נחמן בר יצחק (step 36) is about to explain the enactment differently.

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא יָדְעִי דְּאֶשְׁתָּקַד לָא הֲוָה עוֹמֶר,
phrases.english: But they don't know that last year there was no omer,
so the east lighting up permitted it.
Now that there is an omer, the omer permits it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא יָדְעִי דְּאֶשְׁתָּקַד לָא הֲוָה עוֹמֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the reason from step 31 by explaining why the people's reasoning would be wrong.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: What permits the new grain changes: dawn without a עומר, but only the עומר itself once it is brought.

steps.title: When exactly would the בית המקדש be rebuilt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks when the rebuilding would have to happen for the worry to make sense. If it is rebuilt on the sixteenth, dawn really would permit the grain.
steps.simpleTranslation: When is the בית המקדש rebuilt in this worry? If you say it was rebuilt on the sixteenth, then dawn really did permit the grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is testing the reason it just gave. It asks on what day the בית המקדש would be rebuilt, and rules out the sixteenth right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בית המקדש is only built on the sixteenth, it was not standing at dawn, so the עומר could not be brought. In that case dawn permits the grain, just like last year, and eating would not be a mistake. So the worry from step 31 cannot be about a rebuilding on the sixteenth.

keyTerms.meaning: that it is built (the בית המקדש)
if you say (the גמרא suggests an option, usually to reject it)

phrases.english: When is it that it was built?
phrases.notes: He means the בית המקדש. The גמרא asks what day the rebuilding in step 31 would take place.

phrases.english: If you say that it was built on the sixteenth,
then the east lighting up did permit it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reason given in steps 31-32 by asking what case it describes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason that people might wrongly eat at dawn once the בית המקדש is rebuilt.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it is rebuilt on the sixteenth, no עומר could be brought, so dawn truly permits the grain and there is no mistake.

steps.title: If rebuilt on the fifteenth, midday should permit the grain
steps.stepSummary: So the בית המקדש must be rebuilt on the fifteenth. But then a משנה teaches that people far away may eat from midday on, because the court surely brought the עומר by then. So why forbid the whole day?
steps.simpleTranslation: So it must be rebuilt on the fifteenth. Then from midday on the grain should be allowed. We learned in a משנה: people far away are allowed from midday on, because the court does not delay the עומר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the other option, a rebuilding on the fifteenth. It then attacks it with a משנה that allows the grain from midday.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בית המקדש stood from the fifteenth, the court would bring the עומר early on the sixteenth. The משנה says we can trust them to have done it by midday, so even people far away may eat then. That would make forbidding the entire day of the sixteenth more than needed.

phrases.english: Rather, it means that it was built on the fifteenth.
Then from midday onward let it be permitted,
for we learned in a משנה:
Those who are far away are permitted
from midday onward,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מִתְעַצְּלִים בּוֹ!
phrases.english: because the court is not slow about it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the only remaining option from step 33 and challenges it with a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: Forbidding the grain for the whole sixteenth if the בית המקדש was rebuilt on the fifteenth.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows eating from midday, since the court brings the עומר by then. So the ban should end at midday, not last all day.

steps.title: Rebuilt just before sunset or at night
steps.stepSummary: The worry is when the בית המקדש is rebuilt on the fifteenth right before sunset, or during the night. Then there may be no time to bring the עומר by midday.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only when it was rebuilt on the fifteenth close to sunset. Or, when it was rebuilt at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by narrowing the case to a rebuilding very late on the fifteenth, or during the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the בית המקדש is finished so late, the court cannot get everything ready for the עומר in time, so it may not be brought by midday. Someone eating at midday might eat before the עומר and break the איסור. That is why רבן יוחנן בן זכאי forbade the whole day.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed only for (a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule forbidding חדש for the whole sixteenth fits a case where the בית המקדש is rebuilt so late that the עומר might not be brought by midday.

phrases.english: It is needed only where it was built on the fifteenth
close to sunset.
Or, where it was built at night.
phrases.notes: The night that begins the sixteenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34 by limiting the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a late rebuilding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any rebuilding on the fifteenth would leave plenty of time for the עומר by midday.
steps.terutzMaskana: A rebuilding right before sunset or at night may not leave time, so the whole day must be forbidden.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק begins a different reason
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק starts to give his own explanation of what רבן יוחנן בן זכאי meant. His words continue on the next part of the daf.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new approach. רב נחמן בר יצחק begins to explain the enactment differently, and the rest of his words come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now, the reason was a worry that people would make a mistake once the בית המקדש is rebuilt. רב נחמן בר יצחק is about to offer a different way of reading רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's rule. We need the next lines to see what it is.

keyTerms.meaning: an אמורא who gives a new explanation here
the תנא who made the enactment being discussed

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a second explanation of the enactment, separate from the reason in steps 31-35.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Opening of רב נחמן בר יצחק's different explanation of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי's enactment. It continues in the next lines.
